subject: Offline deployment risk review & next actions
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@biogenix.com>, Tom Hines <tom.hines@biogenix.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: air-gapped deployment areas to validate

Hi Laura / Tom —

Thanks again for the run-through this morning. Per our discovery call, you confirmed Biogenix is leaning toward a private, air-gapped deployment in your on-site data center but still evaluating whether a brief maintenance window with external access for support is acceptable.

I captured the high-level open items we promised to follow up on (see below). Can you confirm or correct where needed so Monica and I can prepare a focused checklist and next steps?

Quick open items (asked on the call):
- Hardware ownership: will Biogenix provide racks + servers, or should Redwood include appliance BOM (we noted a 4U appliance with dual PSU)?
- Firmware/OS patching policy: acceptable cadence for offline patch bundles and whether a staged kernel/firmware upgrade is allowed outside of airgap
- Out-of-band access: do you allow vendor-supplied BMC/network jumpbox during provisioning for initial imaging and verification?
- Spare parts & SLAs: do you have an on-site spares pool or do you want Redwood to include spares in SOW?
- Upgrade window constraints: monthly maintenance windows (2AM–6AM local) vs quarterly larger windows for major OS upgrades

Attached: your network diagram (from Tom) and a draft SOW template we typically adapt for air-gapped installs.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura/Tom confirm the three bullets above (hardware ownership, OOB access, maintenance windows) by EOD Friday
2) Monica will produce an operations checklist and a proposed minimal on-site spares list
3) Ben will surface a recommended offline patch cadence and rollback plan we use for similar deployments

If this looks right, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up early next week to finalize the SOW scope.

Thanks —
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
(rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference)

Attachments: Biogenix_NetworkDiagram_v2.pdf (1.2 MB), Draft_SOW_Redwood.docx (stated as draft)

From: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@biogenix.com>

Cc: Tom Hines <tom.hines@biogenix.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Procurement Team <procure@biogenix.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: air-gapped deployment areas to validate

Rishi —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the high-level responses and adding context:

- Hardware ownership: Biogenix will provide racks and host blades from our preferred vendor (Dell R760s). We will NOT accept vendor-owned appliances in the primary lab cluster, but we can consider a staging appliance for install verification that gets re-imaged and handed over.
- Firmware/OS patching: Strict policy — all updates must be delivered as an offline bundle and approved by our security team. Major firmware upgrades are quarterly and require a 2-week approval window.
- Out-of-band access: Initial imaging can use our temporary jumpbox; we cannot provide external direct BMC access. Redwood engineers will use the jumpbox while on-site and will be escorted.
- Spare parts: Biogenix maintains a 30-day parts pool; we will need Redwood to provide critical spares (PSUs and NVMe) for 90-day coverage in the SOW.
- Upgrade windows: Monthly 02:00–05:00 local for minor patches; major maintenance only during quarterly weekend windows.

We'll review the attached draft SOW and provide markups. Procurement is looped to flag contract timing constraints (Procurement: we need a draft SOW + indicative pricing by next Tue to align with budget cycle).

Quick ask: can Redwood provide a short note (1 page) describing your offline patching process and rollback plan? That will help our security and ops signoff.

Laura Simmons
Director, Infrastructure Ops
Biogenix Therapeutics
(laura.simmons@biogenix.com)

Laura —

Thanks for the fast clarifications. I'll draft the 1-page offline patching/rollback note — key items I plan to include:
- Packaging: tarball with signed manifests & checksums delivered via encrypted USB or escorted transfer
- Installation sequence: verify pre-checks -> stage patches on local image servers -> staged rollout across rack slices -> health checks and KV cache warmups
- Rollback: automated snapshot-based rollback of model/runtime image + database restore plan; dry-run guidance
- Test window requirements: recommended canary on 2 nodes for 48 hrs before full roll

I'll send the note and a suggested spare-parts minimum list by EOD. Also attaching a short case note from a similar air-gapped deploy (anonymized).

Rishi / Ben —

Couple of follow-ups from my infra team after reviewing the network diagram:
1) We need a clear list of required ports between the staging appliance and internal services (DNS, NTP, internal auth).
2) Does Redwood support using an internal pull-mirror for model artifacts (so no outbound egress is required)? If so, what's the sync cadence and artifact signing process?
3) Who owns the rollback steps in an emergency? Biogenix or Redwood? We prefer a runbook where Biogenix ops can trigger a fast rollback.

If you can provide these three items in a short note it will accelerate our security review and procurement.

Tom Hines
Lead Systems Architect
Biogenix Therapeutics

Hi all —

I've started the ops checklist and included an initial spare-parts BOM. High-level notes below (I will drop the checklist to the shared Drive link):
- Required ports: DNS (53), NTP (123), LDAP/AD (389/636) — all must be scoped to internal VLANs only; we recommend restricting staging appliance to a single management VLAN
- Pull-mirror support: yes — Redwood supports a signed artifact pull-mirror model. Recommended sync cadence: nightly, with manual pre-approved immediate sync for urgent patches. Artifacts are signed with an HSM-backed key and we provide verification tooling.
- Rollback responsibility: primary rollback will be a coordinated action; Biogenix triggers the local rollback command (we provide a signed runbook and a Redwood on-call engineer to assist). We can include a 'fast-rollback' playbook in the SOW with clear checkpoints.

Next steps:
- Ben to send the 1-page offline patching and rollback note (target: EOD)
- Rishi to prepare a tailored SOW draft reflecting Biogenix constraints (target: Tue)
- Procurement to confirm budget window (Laura cc'd)

I'll upload the checklist and BOM to the Drive folder and share the link shortly.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
